before.question: List all end-game VP categories, the points for reputation levels 1–7, wealth rounding, and the complete victory tiebreak sequence.
before.expected_answer: Tiles including negative; gentry in hand/discard incl final Fairchild and negatives; remaining objectives; reputation 1,3,6,10,15,21,28 for levels1–7; servants2 each; £200 per1VP rounded down; unused VP cards. Tie: final Fairchild holder, then highest rep level ignoring position, then shared victory.
before.actual_answer: Final VP comes from improvement tiles (including negative printed VP); gentry in hand and discard (including family, negatives, and final Fairchild); fulfilled objectives; reputation levels 1–7 for 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant of any type/location; £1 per £200, rounded down; and retained VP cards’ printed VP. Highest total wins. Ties go to the player with the final Fairchild, then highest reputation level; if still tied, players share victory. Wheel position is irrelevant to ordinary reputation VP and ties.
before.reader_evidence: ‘Final VP’ table and paragraph; wheel position never breaks a final tie.
before.reason: All other requested Q15 facts are supplied, but the wealth scoring states £1 per £200 instead of 1 VP per £200. This is a material wrong scoring unit; the correct round-down instruction does not cure it.

after.reason: The output symbol £ is wrong: the source awards VP, not money. However, this exact phrase is an item governed by the answer’s explicit opening, “Final VP comes from”, in a single end-game scoring enumeration. Its numerator is 1, its divisor is £200 and its downward rounding is express. The surrounding answer supplies the VP-result context, so the written answer determines the same numerical wealth VP computation without needing another answer or the key. It does not separately instruct the player to gain money, spend money or score £1 as a second currency conversion. Thus this is a defective unit label in an otherwise determined scoring expression, rather than a material competing wealth rule. Correct it to “1 VP per £200, rounded down”. This conclusion relies on the actual grammatical scoring context, not a guess about what the writer meant.

scope_boundary.scope: Second-edition base/core, standard multiplayer with reputation levels 1–7, as specified in the supplied summary.
scope_boundary.category_enumeration_requirement: Each of the seven categories must be identifiable. Equivalent labels such as service and servants are acceptable. A category list need not reproduce every qualifying phrase in the key when the answer does not contradict those qualifications.
scope_boundary.category_qualifications: Negative tile and gentry values, hand/discard coverage, final Fairchild inclusion, remaining objectives and retained VP cards clarify category membership. A claim excluding eligible pieces or ignoring negative VP would be a substantive wrong rule. Mere absence of every such detail is not automatically failure of this enumeration question.
scope_boundary.volunteered_rules: Any additional ruling is checked against the source. A materially wrong extra ruling can invalidate an otherwise complete answer. A local unit-label defect may be nonmaterial when the answer’s own surrounding wording fixes the operation, operands and scoring context; this is assessed without assuming authorial intent.
scope_boundary.no_cross_answer_completion: Each answer is judged as standalone; neither receives credit from the other answer, key, evidence label or summary.

after.nonmaterial_text_defect: Original raw wording £1 per £200 is preserved; fresh focused adjudicator finds scoring context fixes VP computation and judges unit label nonmaterial. Full grader11 disagreed and remains preserved.
